I own a Laundry machine sales and service business and I do this bearing and seal job a lot. So here is a little advice for anyone doing this repair. I won’t go into the bearing replacement because it requires a lot more info and the press tool is essential. So, to replace your tub seal only, you will need: a putty knife, a 7/16” socket, a philips screw driver or drill with the philips bit, a wood screw, possibly a car jack and a piece of 2by4 wood cut to approx 21” long. All purpose adhesive which you can buy at most big stores, it’s about $2, I also use some shellack but it’s not essential. So the method: look at the back of your washer, if it has two 1/4” bolts on a green hinge just remove the top screw. Then on the front of the washer where the top meets the base, use your putty knife in the crack, around 6” in from each end there is a catch that you have to push back to release the top of the washer, try lifting the top as you push the putty knife back. Now the top is up, use a pair of pliers that I don’t mention earlier to release the spring catch on the hose at the back of the drum. Then go around the drum cover and release the clips, remove the cover and hose. Use a flat head screw driver and remove the center cap on the wash pulsator. Use the 7/16” socket to remove the bolt, lift the pulsator out, if it’s jammed in there try pushing a screwdriver into the holes close to the bolt and lift. Remove the 6 philips screws holding the tub hub on, be careful because they are soft and you can ruin the screw easily, if you do you will have to drill the screw out. Lift out the two parts of the tub hub. Try lifting the tub out with a helper, if it won’t come out you will need to use the car jack and wood, search YouTube for the method, it’s easier than trying to explain. Once the tub is out you will see the old seal at the base of the shaft. Take the wood screw and screw it in to the edge of the old seal and pull it out with pliers, if it won’t budge try using an extra screw on the other side. Once it’s out, clean up the rim and inspect the bearing. Make sure you grease the inside of the new seal, liberally rub it into the grooves on the INSIDE of the seal. Then holding the seal put a very liberal amount of your adhesive all around the outer rim the the seal, use plenty! Then you can very carefully place the tub seal over the shaft and gently push it down until it has seated. I use a plastic tube and a mallet to seat it fully but you could tap it down gently in a circular motion until it’s pushed right down, then get more adhesive and put it around the top edge where the seal meets the tub. Backtracking a few steps, when you remove the old seal, there is a small weep hole in the 4 o clock position, stick something down the to make sure it’s clean, a straightened paper clip or small screwdriver. Now reassemble the washer and leave the adhesive to cure for 24hrs. The seal will not repair seized bearings, an old seal causes seized bearings so if your washer makes a sound like a bag of rocks or a jet taking off you should replace the bearings too. This job would take me around 30 mins to complete so give yourself 90 mins because I have done hundreds of them.
